newsitem.title: UK: FEATURE-Guinness launches big St Patrick's day promotion.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Guinness launches big St Patrick's day promotion.

text.p: Brewing giant Guinness is launching its biggest ever promotional programme to mark St Patrick's Day on Monday, including helping to create kits to set up "Irish pubs" in places like China or Kazakhstan.
St Patrick Day's -- March 17 -- celebrates the patron saint of Ireland. Guinness says its strong, black stout with a creamy head is basically Ireland's national drink.

"St Patrick's Day is definitely the biggest day for Guinness sales and not just in Ireland but all over the world," Jonathan Miller, a spokesman for Guinness Brewing Worldwide, part of Guinness Plc, told Reuters this week.
"Regular consumers drink more of it and people who may never have tasted it before will often give it a go and join in the celebrations," he said.

St Patrick's Day is celebrated not only in Ireland, but wherever Irish expatriots or those of Irish descent gather. It is an important day for Irish-Americans, who often wear something green to mark the occasion.
"Where there is a St Patrick's Day party, then there is Guinness," said Brendan O'Neill, managing director of Guinness Brewing Worldwide.
The London-based company says it sells ten million glasses of Guinness around the world every day. It is available in 150 countries.

Guinness said it was unsure how many glasses would be drunk this St Patrick's Day, but is spending seven million pounds ($11.1 million) in Britain alone on promotions which include advertising, parties and music festivals.
Guinness drinkers in Filthy MacNasty's Irish bar in north London told Reuters they would be drinking more Guinness than usual to celebrate the event.
"Things usually get a bit out of hand on St Patrick's day, but it's a chance to celebrate my Irish roots," said Michael Kavanagh, an Irishman living in London.
In the United States many of the 40-million-strong Irish-American community will hold parades and festivals.
Guinness said it would hold a competition in the United States to win a pub in Ireland. Some 55,000 people took part in a similar contest in 1996.
This year the prize is ownership of Morrissey's Pub in the town of Cahir in County Tipperary.
Guinness is also sponsoring parties in bars in almost every major European city from Dublin to Moscow as well as in Australia and New Zealand.
IRISH THEME BAR PHENONMENON
Many of the parties will be held in Irish theme bars which Guinness said were becoming increasingly popular around the world.
"The Irish pub has become a phenomenon. You can go into an Irish bar in Russia, Dubai or Fiji and they will be selling Guinness and playing Irish music," said Miller.
To take advantage of consumer interest in Guinness and Irish bars, the company has invested 10 million pounds in an operation that helps individuals set up their own Irish pubs.
The Irish Pub Company designs and builds pubs in Dublin which are then shipped in flat packs to their destination. The pubs cost from 250,000 pounds and there is no shortage of buyers.

"So far there are over 200 of them. An Irish bar was recently opened in Shanghai and we have even received an inquiry from a man who is interested in setting up an Irish bar in Kazakhstan," said Miller.
($ = 0.629 British Pounds Sterling)
